key_insight: CGMap uses distance-resolved graph learning to organize dispersed cancer-related signals into interpretable gene priorities. This helps researchers narrow the list of candidate cancer genes and connect predictions to practical validation.
problem_solved: Cancer-related signals are scattered across biological networks, making it difficult to identify which genes deserve follow-up and explain why they were prioritized.
method: Apply CGMap, a graph-learning framework that distinguishes signals by their distance within a network.
Combine dispersed cancer-related signals to prioritize candidate genes.
Provide an interpretable path from gene hypotheses to candidates for practical validation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CGMap illustrates how graph-based models can produce actionable, interpretable rankings for scientific discovery. Its focus on candidate prioritization connects model outputs with downstream experimental decisions.
visual_elements: Gene-network diagram with concentric distance bands showing nearby and more distant signals.
Pipeline: dispersed cancer signals → CGMap → prioritized genes → validation.
Ranked candidate-gene list with highlighted top priorities.
Zoom-in panel tracing network signals contributing to a selected gene's priority.
paper_title: Interpretable distance-resolved graph learning for cancer gene priority screening
paper_authors: Chenhao Wang, Shidong Xu, Li Tang, Gang Luo, Yongchang Zhang
